STEP 1 - Scene: This is a small snack of roasted almonds on a white square plate, photographed from above (near top-down view). The plate is slightly angled but its shape is close to square.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square side plate, roughly 20 cm across. Area ≈ 20 x 20 ≈ 400 cm² (using the plate's outer width; the rounded corners reduce this slightly, so use ~330 cm² as the effective area for the cover estimate). Almonds are about 2.5 cm long and 1.5 cm wide, so the plate-to-almond scale is consistent with a 20 cm plate.

STEP 3 - Items: One food: whole roasted almonds, about 20 pieces. No visible oil or sauce beyond a light residue.

STEP 4 - Area: The almond cluster covers roughly 20% of the plate's visible area (about 65 cm²) in a loose pile.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height is about 1.2 cm on average (almonds are piled, roughly one to two layers). Volume ≈ 65 cm² x 1.2 cm ≈ 78 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole nuts have a bulk density around 0.5–0.6 g/ml when piled with gaps. 78 ml x 0.55 ≈ 43 g. Cross-check: 20 almonds at about 1.2 g each ≈ 24 g, so the volume-based estimate is a bit high; take a middle value of about 35 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted almonds ≈ 600 kcal per 100 g. 35 g x 6.0 ≈ 210 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 20 almonds is a typical small handful, roughly 30–40 g and about 200 kcal, which is plausible for what is visible.
